clue.text: With passion, speak to renounce one's right?

definitions.meaning: to orate or deliver words in a passionate, rhetorical manner
whimsically, to un-claim: DE- as a reversing prefix on a claim, a right one asserts

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether impassioned oratory amounts to giving up some entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage, hence the question mark: DE- (undoing) attached to CLAIM, a right asserted.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate in a theatrical, emotional way is the standard dictionary sense of this verb.

clue.text: Make note to show uncritical fondness

parts.note: to do is to make
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Write something down to express adoring affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish excessive, blind affection on someone is uncritical fondness.

clue.text: Clothes line fixed by friend from Oz

indicators.note: fixed by suggests being set in place by something enclosing, so one letter is lodged inside

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate

explanation.surface: An Australian mate repairs a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' is Australia; clobber is British slang for clothes and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for one's gear or garments, so it means clothes.

clue.text: Walk miles to keep fit? The opposite

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so one word holds another
the opposite tells us to swap the roles: the fit word holds the miles letter, not vice versa

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Advice to walk many miles to stay in shape, then a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep fit' looks like exercise advice; 'The opposite' reverses who holds whom.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll is a kind of walk, as a verb a gentle saunter.

clue.text: Skimpy garment being worn, fine when covered by skirt

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed within, so the skirt word goes round the others

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
a garment being worn is on
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A revealing outfit, acceptable provided a skirt goes over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A topless swimsuit, just the bottom half of a bikini, is a very skimpy garment.

clue.text: Greek hero, half-lost, struggled on towards America

indicators.note: half of the word is lost, so only the front portion of the synonym survives

parts.note: to struggle on is to persevere, past tense persevered
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A legendary warrior, partly defeated, battles onward toward the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled on' is the synonym that gets cut in half; 'towards' is only a link placing the country after it.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the mythical slayer of Medusa, one of the great heroes of Greek legend.

clue.text: Being model officer, good going after crime

indicators.note: going after means following, so the good letter comes after crime

parts.note: PO is a petty officer
a sin is a wrong or crime

explanation.surface: An exemplary officer who, being good, chases down crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model sits still for a portrait, so acting as a model means holding a pose.

clue.text: Meeting announced to follow about poor economic situation

indicators.note: to follow puts the sounded word after the short word for about

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so a word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a session is a meeting of a body

explanation.surface: A meeting is announced to discuss a weak economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump, a period of falling output, is a poor economic situation.

clue.text: I eat well and I smoke after exercise is over

indicators.note: after places the I and smoke pieces behind the exercise piece
is over means turned over, so in a down clue the letters are reversed

parts.note: PE is physical exercise, physical education
taken as written
to cure fish is to smoke it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to eating heartily and smoking once the workout is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoke' suggests a cigarette but means CURE, as of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet, someone who takes pleasure in fine food, can say this of himself.

clue.text: Not shifting goods for sale at whisky producer's?

parts.note: a shop's stock is its goods for sale
a still is the apparatus that distils whisky

explanation.surface: Merchandise that won't sell at a distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not shifting' pretends to describe unsold stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely motionless means not moving or shifting at all.

clue.text: No mobster forged brass

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters of the words before are remade

explanation.surface: A gangster didn't counterfeit any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like slang for money alongside the forger, but it is the orchestral section.
explanation.definitionFit: These slide instruments belong to the brass section of an orchestra, so are examples of brass.

clue.text: Companion wearing old cotton fabric

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
wearing a hat means having it on, i.e. in it

explanation.surface: A partner dressed in an old-fashioned cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This twilled cotton cloth is used for casual trousers, so it is a cotton fabric.

clue.text: Singles on holiday love to score

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
singles are ones
love is nil, and a duck is a cricketer's score of nil

explanation.surface: Unattached people on vacation hope to find romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero; to end it is to make one's first run.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket idiom meaning to make one's first run, hence to get off the mark and score at last.

clue.text: Didn't stop at unfashionable town in Kent

parts.note: passe means out of date or unfashionable
Dover is a port town in Kent, the English county

explanation.surface: A train skipped a dowdy Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Dover is its Channel port.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by a place without halting, to omit or ignore, means not to stop at it.

clue.text: I'm overcome by a colleague showing resentment

indicators.note: overcome by suggests being covered or enveloped, so the first word goes inside the next

parts.note: a crony is a close companion or associate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being overwhelmed by a co-worker who bears a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness and ill feeling are what both words convey; they are near synonyms.

clue.text: To north of lake, mange affected lots of animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of means placed above, so the anagram precedes the lake
affected means altered, so the letters of mange are rearranged

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Animals north of a lake catch a skin disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild animals kept for show is a zoo-like assembly, lots of beasts.

clue.text: One reaches home after following A1

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the abbreviation that comes earlier

parts.note: F is the usual abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral one
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone gets back home after tailing a man called Al.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Al' looks like a man's name; it is A1, meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A1 means first-class or excellent, as does the superlative 'best of all'.

clue.text: From Mediterranean island head off little whale

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed from the word for little

parts.note: small means little
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A small whale heads away from an island in the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: It's small and shiny

parts.note: 'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA
tiny means small

explanation.surface: A curt verdict on some object: compact and gleaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention from 1920s slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a glossy sheen like silk fabric looks shiny.

clue.text: Who might be held up as ace drinker?

definitions.text: Who might be held up as ace drinker?

indicators.note: held up means raised, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: tops means first-rate or ace
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Asks who could be singled out as a champion boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a habitual drunkard, a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Fellow consumer about to join party at pub reeling

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: reeling means spinning round, so the words that follow are turned back to front

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A drinking companion is about to join a party at a pub, already staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow consumer' is a grim joke: one who consumes his fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater literally consumes his fellow humans, so is a consumer of his fellows.

clue.text: Fine is a form of punishment

definitions.meaning: first-rate, excellent, as in a cracking or terrific performance

explanation.surface: Someone claims a penalty payment is a kind of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' pretends to be a monetary penalty; it means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for excellent, and also a beating with a strap, so both senses fit.

clue.text: For a start, things always look up, so persist

indicators.note: up means reading upward, so in a down clue the letters are reversed
for a start means the first letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: a peek is a look

explanation.surface: Optimistic advice: things are improving at last, so carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep working doggedly at a task means to persist with it.

clue.text: Dodgy bling dealers import European fashion brand

indicators.note: to import is to bring something in, so a letter is brought into the fodder
dodgy means suspect or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shady jewellery traders bring in goods from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges BLING DEALERS once E is brought in by 'import'.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier's name tag on clothing marks a fashion brand of prestige.

clue.text: Islanders become restless, rising against brutal leader

indicators.note: against means next to, so the two parts sit side by side
leader means the first letter of brutal
rising means going up, so in a down clue the letters read upward

parts.note: to stir is to move or become restless

explanation.surface: Islanders grow agitated and rise against a cruel ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Great Britain, an island nation, are islanders.

clue.text: Opponent involved in unpleasant incident

indicators.note: involved in means contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An adversary was part of a nasty episode.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is against something is an opponent of it, a noun as well as a preposition.

clue.text: Malicious person in struggle to seize power, facing resistance

indicators.note: facing means standing next to, so the next letter is placed alongside
seizing something means grasping it, so the struggle word takes another inside

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
P is the physics symbol for power
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A spiteful character fights to grab control despite opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is figuratively a treacherous, spiteful person, as in nursing a snake in one's bosom.

clue.text: Page at front of publication about dictator's ultimate downfall

indicators.note: at front of places the page letter before the rest
about means surrounding, so the publication word goes round a letter

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter of the dictator is taken

explanation.surface: A page at the front of a magazine covering the tyrant's eventual fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin or damnation, utter destruction, is a downfall in the strongest sense.

clue.text: Renegotiate retirement

definitions.meaning: playfully read as to treat again, since to treat is to negotiate
withdrawal or seclusion, as to a quiet refuge

explanation.surface: Two words: a contract revision and someone leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal from activity, or a secluded place to withdraw to, is a retirement; RE-TREAT is treating again.

clue.text: Weapon in rear part of carriage pulled back by donkey

indicators.note: by means beside, so the donkey word sits next to the rest

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: pulled back means drawn backwards, so these letters are reversed
only the rear part of the word carriage is wanted, so its front four letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A spear found at the back of a cart being hauled by a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples, hence a weapon.
